sources.note: Gives the teacher in on-policy self-distillation access to each completed student rollout and its verified outcome, adapting it to preserve behaviour on successes and redirect failures toward verified success, while the student keeps a prefix-only interface it can actually deploy.
sources.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation

sources.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
sources.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

result.definition: The difference between what a teacher model assigns to a token or trajectory and what the student does -- used across these sources as a signal rather than as a loss. Two papers convert it into credit: one re-scores a search agent's own sampled tokens under a teacher that has been shown the instance's supporting evidence and uses the detached gap to nudge the group-relative advantage up or down on search and answer tokens only, adding no distillation loss and changing nothing at inference; another turns token-level gaps into turn-level credit by recursively updating a Bayesian belief in log-odds space. The third source shows the gap has a direction that matters and that a symmetric objective destroys: student-excess tokens, generated by the student but given near-zero teacher probability, produce log-ratio corrections that grow unbounded and destabilise the update, while student-deficit tokens, preferred by the teacher but rarely sampled, are never reached at all -- 95.5 percent of deficit positions have under a one percent chance of appearing in sampled supervision. A fourth constraint comes from the privileged-teacher work: forward-KL distillation provably targets the teacher's conditional mean given the prefix, so the part of a teacher's advantage that depends on information the student will not have is formally untransferable, and measuring the teacher's success measures something the student cannot inherit.
